content: The Duke University Health System integrates the Duke University School of Medicine, the Duke University School of Nursing, the Duke Clinic, and its affiliated hospitals into a comprehensive network dedicated to research, clinical care, and education. Duke University Hospital In 1925, James B. Duke allocated $4 million to establish the Duke University School of Medicine, the Duke University School of Nursing, and Duke University Hospital, with the goal of advancing healthcare in the Carolinas and across the United States. Construction of the hospital and medical school began in 1927, and the hospital officially opened to patients on July 21, 1930. On its first day, 17 out of its 400 available beds were occupied. In 1936, Dr. Julian Deryl Hart, a surgeon at Duke, pioneered the use of ultraviolet lights in operating rooms to eliminate airborne pathogens. In 1956, Duke surgeons became the first to employ systemic hypothermia during cardiac surgery, a technique that has since become a global standard. The institution was renamed the Duke University Medical Center in 1957. In 1963, the Duke University School of Medicine admitted its first African American student. In the 1990s, Duke geneticists developed a rapid three-minute test capable of screening newborns for over 30 metabolic disorders simultaneously, a test now widely used across the United States. In 1992, Duke performed its first lung transplant and its first combined heart-lung transplant. Duke Children's Hospital and Health Center Duke Children's Hospital & Health Center specializes in providing medical care for patients ranging from newborns to young adults. The facility includes both a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and a pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). The McGovern-Davison Children's Health Center, located within the hospital, offers outpatient services across more than 28 pediatric medical and surgical specialties. Additionally, Duke Children's provides primary care services at multiple locations within Durham County. The Duke Children's Miracle Network raises unrestricted funds to support the hospital's research initiatives, clinical care programs, and family support services. These funds are part of the broader Children's Miracle Network fundraising efforts. Durham Regional Hospital Durham Regional Hospital delivers a range of healthcare services, including inpatient, outpatient, surgical, and emergency care. The hospital features a Level II intensive care nursery, the Durham Regional Rehabilitation Institute, and the Davis Ambulatory Surgical Center. Newborn care at this facility is provided by physicians affiliated with Duke Children's Hospital. Historically, the hospital was known as Lincoln Hospital and Watts Hospital before adopting its current name. Duke Raleigh Hospital Duke Raleigh Hospital became part of the Duke University Health System in 1998. Originally named Mary Elizabeth Hospital when it opened in 1914, it was later renamed Raleigh Community Hospital and relocated to its current site on Wake Forest Road in 1978. The hospital has 186 beds and a medical staff comprising over 500 physicians. Newborn care at Duke Raleigh Hospital is provided by physicians from Duke Children's Hospital. Additionally, Duke Children's Consultative Services of Raleigh extends specialized pediatric care from Duke Children's Hospital to the Raleigh area. In 2004, the hospital experienced a significant error when hydraulic fluid was mistakenly used instead of detergents to sterilize surgical instruments.
